decisions.reason: It is close to the firm's core airport-operations software and systems business, the firm has strong in-house R&D and integration capabilities to keep learning from it, and its continued standalone presentation in 2024 signals commitment and traction.

As an apron connectivity module it builds directly on the firm's established operational platform knowledge, and the move from a mention in 2023 to its own page in 2024 suggests successful assimilation and commercialization.

Although billing software is somewhat less central than airside control products, it still builds on the firm's integrated airport data and software offer, and the stronger 2024 website presence points to enough promise to retain it.

This product fits especially well with the firm's installed equipment experience, monitoring, maintenance, and digitalization strategy, so absorptive capacity is high and removal within a year is unlikely.
